content:
Last Friday (21st), during the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance case, a woman queuing to observe the hearing was taken onto a police vehicle in the early hours. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was charged with three offences: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or intentionally obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "with seditious intent."

Around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. While waiting, a plainclothes police officer pointed to a woman in the queue, claiming her "clothing was suspected of carrying seditious intent," and subsequently took her onto a police vehicle. While officers were taking the woman away, multiple officers repeatedly asked reporters to leave, saying they would "take you to the press area," and at the same time extended the orange cordon in the direction of Ying Wa Street. Once the woman had boarded the police vehicle, they put away the cordon. A "court observation volunteer" who was standing near the woman in the queue that day said the woman was wearing a black T-shirt printed with Japanese text.

集誌社 (The Collective) enquired with the police regarding the reason for the woman's removal and whether she had been arrested. The police replied this morning (24th) that during a security operation in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on charges of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or intentionally obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "with seditious intent," and that she is currently being detained for investigation.
